summary: Interpreting receipt 02448a3b3ab64a108a72d3555345f6b1, in which the corrected exploration injected membership changes and completed cleanly. Seed 11 accepted 8 of 27 attempted conf-change proposals and ran 103 proposals, 15 campaigns, 15 transfer requests, 204 messages delivered, 178 dropped and 16 distinct applied indexes; seed 23 accepted 2 of 18 attempts with 91 proposals, 4 campaigns, 8 transfers, 257 delivered, 177 dropped and 14 applied indexes. Both summaries report zero violations and the stream contains no safety_violation, conf_change_apply_panic or conf_change_unmarshal event, so one leader per term, per-node immutability of applied entries, cross-node agreement for an index, per-node commit monotonicity and completeness at each leadership transition held across configurations that actually changed. The interpretation is recorded with conclusion holds and no defect judgment, with explicit limits: two seeds and 300 steps, snapshots, restarts and crash-stop faults excluded, only 8 and 2 accepted membership changes so the configuration axis is sampled thinly, loss keeping commit progress low, safety-style monitors only, and non-reproducible sampling due to randomized election timeouts. The four completeness reports seen earlier in local testing are now explained as a monitor artifact rather than target behaviour: completeness is owed only by a newly elected leader for entries committed before its election, and the restricted predicate did not fire here. Separately, a decisive positive control was prepared and verified locally for the primary finding: with the member still an outgoing voter in a joint configuration that is never left, its proposal returned in 0 ms and committed on all three nodes, isolating the disappearance of the local progress entry as the necessary premise of the held-proposal effect rather than any configuration change.
